First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x(\operatorname{csc}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the identity $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}$ to further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{2\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}-\frac{2\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =2-2{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity ${sin}^{2}⁡x=1-{cos}^{2}⁡x$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x(\operatorname{csc}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x)=2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$
